newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends strong despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends strong despite profit-taking.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICALS
Oct (3rd pos) 1,269 rgt/tonne Aug (south) 1,295
Open/Hi/Low 1,250/1,272/1,250 Prev close 1,280
Prev settlement 1,244 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES -Prices ended strong despite intermittent bouts of profit-taking, due to bullish PORLA July crop data, a weak ringgit and Aug 1-15 exports from SGS. Trading was volatile, with players optimistic that Oct could test 1,280 rgt next week. Oct seen well supported at 1,250.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL- Also firmed in line with futures, with more refiners buying seen among CPOs and selected products.

He added: "I am very positive that the market can move higher next week and test the resistance of 1,280 ringgit (October futures). It is good enough that prices could break the 1,270 and rose to a high of 1,272 ringgit."
At the close, the October futures contract closed 25 ringgit higher at 1,269 ringgit ($456.80) a tonne.
Prices rallied strongly in volatile trading after Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licening Authority (PORLA) announced a bullish July palm oil crop report.
PORLA, which announced the data after the close of the morning market, said end-July palm oil stocks was at 769,275 tonnes against the 789,806 tonnes at end June.

July palm oil exports totalled 715,906 tonnes against 622,210 in June. It also gave some bearish data on production, saying July output rose 5.27 percent to 833,159 tonnes. But traders said this did not matter much to the market.
"Not only the bullish PORLA stock and export numbers, the local market also helped by a weak ringgit against the U.S. dollar," a trader said.
The ringgit, which fell more than 13 percent in value against the US dollar in the last month, hit an all-time low of 2.81 to a dollar at 0500 GMT. But it recovered to 2.7780 to a dollar at 0900 GMT.
"It appears the market is going to stay speculative and strong if the ringgit stays like this," said a trader.
Traders were also concerned about the movement of the Indonesian rupiah which fell to a historic low again.
"There will be more demand for their palm as prices would be more competitive compared with Malaysia," another trader said.
Cargo surveyor SGS (M) Bhd''s August 1-15 palm oil exports a at 312,757 tonnes against 307,536 tonnes was cited as a supportive factor behind the market rise.
The physical sector saw more refiners' buying and active covering, traders said.
Physicals saw Aug (south) offered at 1,295 ringgit against bids of 1,290. Aug (central) also offered at 1,285 against bids of 1,275 with trades done at 1,270 and 1,275.
Sept (south) saw offers at 1,300 ringgit against bids of 1,292.50. Sept (central) was offered at 1,290 against 1,285 with trades done at 1,280 and 1,282.
In refined palm oil, Aug/Sept RBD palm oil was offered at $492.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Oct/Nov/Dec at $490.
Aug/Sept RBD palm olein saw offers at $530, Oct/Nov/Dec at $525. Aug was traded at $530, Sept at $527.50 and $525, and Oct/Nov/Dec at $522.50.
Aug/Dec RBD palm stearin was offered $362.50 a tonne. Aug/Sept RBD palm fatty acid distillate saw offers at $287.50.
